column11: Kisqali, CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand): $775,493,707.49 over 8,782 beneficiaries = $88,304.68 per beneficiary a year. That per-beneficiary figure is the book's anchor on a CMS series, the basis amgn_abp_206.csv carries. For scale, the labelled-year gross is $238,114: the same CMS file gives $775,493,707.49 over 2,674,696 dosage units = $289.94 a 200 mg tablet, and a labelled year at the advanced-breast-cancer dose of 600 mg daily (three 200 mg tablets) for 21 of every 28 days is 63 tablets a cycle x 365/28 = 821.25 tablets (Kisqali prescribing information, NDA 209092, label effective 2026-07-01)
column12: a price per patient treated in a year, not per full year on drug, and that is what makes it consistent with discontinuation_pct: $88,304.68 / $238,114 = 0.3709 is exactly the share of a labelled year the stopping row derives from dosage units per beneficiary. Pairing the full labelled-year figure with the same 0.6291 would count the shortfall twice, once in the price and once in the stopping rate. Part D spending is gross of manufacturer rebates, which gross_to_net_pct takes off

column11: measured on Kisqali's own patients: CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand), 2,674,696 dosage units over 8,782 beneficiaries = 304.57 of the 200 mg tablets a beneficiary. A labelled year at 600 mg daily for 21 of every 28 days is 63 tablets a cycle and 365/28 = 13.04 cycles, 821.25 tablets (Kisqali prescribing information, NDA 209092), so a beneficiary averages 0.3709 of a labelled year on drug and 1 - 0.3709 = 0.6291. The ratio across 2020 to 2024 is 0.422, 0.409, 0.361, 0.345 and 0.371
column12: the Opdivo method (amgn_abp_206.csv, bmy_opdivo.csv), measured on the same beneficiaries the price above is quoted on, which is the point: the engine's stock is then the count of beneficiaries that price applies to. Two reasons this overstates stopping. (1) Dose reduction is counted as stopping. The same file gives 52,578 claims over 8,782 beneficiaries = 5.99 fills a beneficiary, which against 13.04 cycles is 0.459 of a year, and the gap between 0.459 and 0.371 is the average claim carrying 50.9 tablets rather than 63 - ribociclib is dose-reduced for neutropenia and QT prolongation, and the 400 mg early-breast-cancer dose approved in September 2024 is two tablets a day, not three. (2) Medicare beneficiary counts nearly doubled in 2024 (4,543 to 8,782), so a large share of the denominator started part-way through the year. The case for far lower: MONALEESA-2 (NCT01958021) reports median progression-free survival not reached, 95% CI 19.3 months to not reached, for Kisqali plus letrozole (Kisqali prescribing information, Table 19), and a median of 19.3 months at a constant hazard is 35% a year. That figure measures a trial cohort's time to progression; this one measures a year's treated Medicare patients, and it is the second that pairs with a per-beneficiary price

column11: already approved. The KISQALI indications read 'adults' in both settings, not women: 'the adjuvant treatment of adults with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative stage II and III early breast cancer at high risk of recurrence' and 'the treatment of adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer' (NDA 209092, label effective 2026-07-01, openFDA drug/label). Three further places in the same label settle it. Section 2.1 gives the dose for men: 'Pre/perimenopausal women, or men, treated with the combination KISQALI plus an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant, should be treated with a luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) agonist according to current clinical practice'. Section 6.1 reports the safety of KISQALI in men (n = 39). Section 14 carries COMPLEEMENT-1 (NCT02941926), an open-label study of ribociclib in men with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, and records a median duration of exposure of 20.8 months
column12: the reported revenue already contains these patients, so no pool is seeded and nothing is added. NCT05827081 is a Phase IIIb study of ribociclib plus endocrine therapy in early breast cancer, an indication Kisqali has held since September 2024; its NATALEE predecessor enrolled 19 men, which the label states. The brief's age-extension exception does not apply here - there is no age or sex the label excludes, so there are no patients outside the revenue to price
